reasons: Both are strong, near-equivalent runbooks: trigger, numbered steps, explicit ban on touching pg_wal, pg_replication_slots diagnosis, clear escalation to Andrey. Both also include an emergency pg_drop_replication_slot step for the on-call person, gated on Andrey's prior approval, so both only partly meet the no-drop requirement, and neither gives an explicit rollback for the connector restart. B edges ahead for non-DBA usability: it shows sample command output, uses a simple Use% severity table in place of A's rate arithmetic, explains why sudo -u postgres is needed and tells Andrey outright to delete the drop step if he does not approve it; its only weakness is an untagged output block.
